q-343663.name: Question 1
q-343663.problem:
Consider the boundary value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+3y=f(x)
$$

on $[-2,2]$, where $f$ is $4$-periodic and odd. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution ${y}_{p}?$$\,$
${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
q-343663.worked_solution:
Because $f$ is $4$-periodic on $[-2,2]$, we have $L=2$, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis 

$$
cos\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\,\text{and}\,sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Next, since $f$ is odd, its Fourier series contains only sine terms. For a second-order equation with no ${y}^{′}$ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an odd function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for ${y}_{p}$ is a sine series:

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$

q-343663.html:
Question 1
?
Consider the boundary value problem y″+3y=f(x) on [−2,2], where f is 4-periodic and odd. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution yp? yp(x)=
∑n=0∞ansin⁡(nπx4)
∑n=0∞ansin⁡(nπx4)
∑n=1∞bncos⁡(nπx4)
∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nπx2)
∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nπx2)

Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Because f is 4-periodic on [−2,2], we have L=2, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis cos(nπx2)andsin(nπx2).

Next, since f is odd, its Fourier series contains only sine terms. For a second-order equation with no y′ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an odd function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for yp is a sine series: yp(x)=∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nπx2)

q-344278.name: Question 2
q-344278.problem:
Consider the boundary value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+2y=f(x)
$$

on $[-4,4]$, where $f$ is $8$-periodic and even. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution ${y}_{p}?$$\,$
${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
q-344278.worked_solution:
Because $f$ is $8$-periodic on $[-4,4]$, we have $L=4$, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{4})\,\text{and}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{4}).
$$

Next, since $f$ is even, its Fourier series contains only cosine terms. For a second-order equation with no ${y}^{′}$ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an even function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for ${y}_{p}$ is a cosine series:

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{4})
$$

Question 2
?
Consider the boundary value problem y″+2y=f(x) on [−4,4], where f is 8-periodic and even. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution yp? yp(x)=
∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nπx4)
∑n=1∞ancos⁡(nπx8)
∑n=0∞bnsin⁡(nπx8)
∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nπx4)
∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nπx4)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Because f is 8-periodic on [−4,4], we have L=4, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis cos⁡(nπx4)andsin⁡(nπx4).

Next, since f is even, its Fourier series contains only cosine terms. For a second-order equation with no y′ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an even function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for yp is a cosine series: yp(x)=∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nπx4)

q-344280.problem:
Consider the boundary value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{1}{2}\,y=f(x)
$$

on $[-2,2]$, where $f$ is $4$-periodic and even. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution ${y}_{p}?$$\,$
${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
q-344280.worked_solution:
Because $f$ is $4$-periodic on $[-2,2]$, we have $L=2$, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\,\text{and}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Next, since $f$ is even, its Fourier series contains only cosine terms. For a second-order equation with no ${y}^{′}$ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an even function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for ${y}_{p}$ is a cosine series:

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$

Question 3
?
Consider the boundary value problem y″+12y=f(x) on [−2,2], where f is 4-periodic and even. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution yp? yp(x)=
∑n=1∞ancos⁡(nπx4)
∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nπx2)
∑n=1∞ancos⁡(nπx4)
∑n=0∞bnsin⁡(nπx4)
∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(nπx2)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Because f is 4-periodic on [−2,2], we have L=2, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis cos⁡(nπx2)andsin⁡(nπx2).

Next, since f is even, its Fourier series contains only cosine terms. For a second-order equation with no y′ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an even function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for yp is a cosine series: yp(x)=∑n=0∞ancos⁡(nπx2)

q-344285.name: Question 4
q-344285.problem:
Consider the boundary value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+4y=f(x)
$$

on $[-\frac{3}{2},\frac{3}{2}]$, where $f$ is $3$-periodic and even. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution ${y}_{p}?$$\,$
${y}_{p}(x)=$
{{field-1}}
q-344285.worked_solution:
Because $f$ is $3$-periodic on $[-\frac{3}{2},\frac{3}{2}]$, we have $L=\frac{3}{2}$, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2n\pi x}{3})\,\text{and}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2n\pi x}{3}).
$$

Next, since $f$ is even, its Fourier series contains only cosine terms. For a second-order equation with no ${y}^{′}$ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an even function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for ${y}_{p}$ is a cosine series:

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2n\pi x}{3})
$$

q-344285.html:
Question 4
?
Consider the boundary value problem y″+4y=f(x) on [−32,32], where f is 3-periodic and even. Which Fourier-series form is appropriate for a particular solution yp? yp(x)=
∑n=0∞ancos⁡(2nπx3)
∑n=1∞ancos⁡(nπx3)
∑n=0∞ancos⁡(2nπx3)
∑n=0∞bnsin⁡(nπx3)
∑n=1∞bnsin⁡(2nπx3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Because f is 3-periodic on [−32,32], we have L=32, so Fourier series on this interval use the basis cos⁡(2nπx3)andsin⁡(2nπx3).

Next, since f is even, its Fourier series contains only cosine terms. For a second-order equation with no y′ (damping) term, the particular solution inherits this property and is also an even function.

Therefore, the appropriate form for yp is a cosine series: yp(x)=∑n=0∞ancos⁡(2nπx3)

q-344326.name: Question 5
q-344326.problem:
Consider the boundary value problem

$$
{y}^{″}+10y=f(x),\,{y}^{′}(0)=0,\,{y}^{′}(1)=6
$$

where $f(x)$ is $4$-periodic and odd. Select the missing part in the solution of the BVP, where the infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution ${y}_{p}$ of the differential equation.

*Hint: In this specific problem, the forcing function $f(x)$ is chosen such that the particular solution ${y}_{p}$ satisfies ${y}_{p}^{′}(0)=0$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}(1)=0.$*

$$
y(x)∼{{field-1}}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$
q-344326.worked_solution:
We write the solution as $y={y}_{c}+{y}_{p}$, where ${y}_{c}$ solves the homogeneous equation and ${y}_{p}$ is a particular solution.

First, solve the homogeneous equation ${y}^{″}+10y=0.$ Its general solution is

$$
{y}_{c}(x)=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{10}x)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{10}x).
$$

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
{y}^{′}(x)=-A\sqrt{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{10}x)+B\sqrt{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{10}x)+{y}_{p}^{′}(x).
$$

Now, we use the hint. Since ${y}_{p}^{′}(0)=0$ and ${y}_{p}^{′}(1)=0$, we have

$$
{y}^{′}(0)={y}_{c}^{′}(0)\,\text{and}\,{y}^{′}(1)={y}_{c}^{′}(1).
$$

Next, we apply the boundary conditions. 

- Use ${y}^{′}(0)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(0) & =0+B\sqrt{10}(1)+{y}_{p}^{′}(0) \\ 0 & =B\sqrt{10}+0 \\ B & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, ${y}_{c}(x)=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{10}x).$

- Use ${y}^{′}(1)=6$ with $B=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(1) & =-A\sqrt{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{10})+{y}_{p}^{′}(1) \\ 6 & =-A\sqrt{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{10})+0 \\ A & =-\frac{6}{\sqrt{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{10})}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is

$$
y(x)∼-\frac{6}{\sqrt{10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{10})}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\sqrt{10}x)+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}sin\,(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Consider the boundary value problem y″+10y=f(x),y′(0)=0,y′(1)=6 where f(x) is 4-periodic and odd. Select the missing part in the solution of the BVP, where the infinite sum on the right-hand side below represents a particular solution yp of the differential equation.

Hint: In this specific problem, the forcing function f(x) is chosen such that the particular solution yp satisfies yp′(0)=0 and yp′(1)=0.

−610sin⁡(10)cos⁡(10x)
610sin⁡(10)sin⁡(10x)
−610sin⁡(10)cos⁡(10x)
610sin⁡(10)cos⁡(10x)
−610cos⁡(10)cos⁡(10x)
y(x)∼{(610sin⁡(10)sin⁡(10x))(S0)}+∑n=1∞bnsin(nπx2).
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We write the solution as y=yc+yp, where yc solves the homogeneous equation and yp is a particular solution.

First, solve the homogeneous equation y″+10y=0. Its general solution is yc(x)=Acos⁡(10x)+Bsin⁡(10x).

Computing the derivative, we get y′(x)=−A10sin⁡(10x)+B10cos⁡(10x)+yp′(x).

Now, we use the hint. Since yp′(0)=0 and yp′(1)=0, we have y′(0)=yc′(0)andy′(1)=yc′(1).

Next, we apply the boundary conditions.

  • Use y′(0)=0: y′(0)=0+B10(1)+yp′(0)0=B10+0B=0 So, yc(x)=Acos⁡(10x).

  • Use y′(1)=6 with B=0: y′(1)=−A10sin⁡(10)+yp′(1)6=−A10sin⁡(10)+0A=−610sin⁡(10)

Therefore, the solution is y(x)∼−610sin⁡(10)cos⁡(10x)+∑n=1∞bnsin(nπx2).
